items.note: Editor says the Pānāhedā prasasti in its description of kings resembles the Udaipur and Nagpur prasastis (Nos. 24 and 33).
Pānāhedā prasasti lists the main line of Paramāra rulers of Mālava down to Jayasiṃha I, then the subordinate branch ending with Maṇḍalīka.
Legend of the Paramāra hero created by Vasishtha who recovered Viśvāmitra's cow is found in the Udaipur prasasti for the first time in epigraphic records.
Pānāhedā prasasti verses on Siyaka II, Muñja, Sindhurāja, Bhoja and Jayasiṃha; editor judges the Jayasiṃha world-conquest statement conventional and historically worthless.
Reference to Siyaka's expedition sacking the Rāshṭrakūṭa capital in 972-73 A.C., as seen in the editor's treatment of the Udaipur prāśastī.
